verdict.rationale: Clerk's first-party remote MCP server exposes account tools that let users "create and configure applications, manage users, and set up production instances" from AI clients such as Claude, Cursor, and Copilot. That means users can operate Clerk itself through natural-language prompts, not just retrieve SDK snippets. The CLI connects this MCP server in one command, and agent registration can provision accountless apps. Missing for 10: a native natural-language interface in Clerk's own dashboard, detailed documentation of the account-tool scope beyond a single line, and independent or hands-on corroboration that operating Clerk via prompts works reliably.
